title: The sheaf dual-tensor-Hom morphism is the closed categorical comparison
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and M,N any O_X-modules. Write M^\vee=\mathcal Hom(M,O_X). The morphism M^\vee\otimes N\to\mathcal Hom(M,N) defined by sheafifying the presheaf map phi tensor n mapped to (m mapped to phi(m)n) equals the canonical closed-category map obtained by transposing the evaluation-and-multiplication morphism M\otimes(M^\vee\otimes N)\to N.

source.place: Canonical tensor-Hom morphism, generalized to target N; the bridge compares its two library constructions.

proof.text: Compute uncurry of an arbitrary sheafified presheaf map using SheafOfModules.uncurry_eq_tensorHomEquiv_symm, the sheafification hom equivalence, the adjunction triangle identity, and naturality of the sheafification tensorator. This is the private proved helper dualTensorHom_transport.

Unfold PresheafOfModules.dualTensorHom and cancel homObjEquiv with its inverse. Expand the sheaf evaluation using ihom_ev_app and Adjunction.homEquiv_counit. The private proved helper dualTensorHom_pairing transports associativity, evaluation, and the left unitor along the strong monoidal sheafification functor, using its associativity and left-unit coherence laws. Apply uncurry_injective and specialize the resulting site-level comparison to X.sheaf.

proof_origin.note: The proof expands the existing presheaf comparison and sheaf tensor-Hom adjunction, then uses strong monoidal coherence. Every helper is proved privately; no auxiliary sorry or additional DAG dependency remains.
